title: Made my first game demo inspired by Inscryption, but biology-themed. Looking for feedback!
author: MDInformatics
selftext:
**Game Title:** Inoculum

**Playable link:** (https://inoculumcardgame.itch.io/inoculum) (better quality link in comments)

**Platform:** Web Browser

**Description:** Hey y’all. Played Inscryption a few months ago and just couldn’t get phase 1 out of my head. So for some time I’ve been working on a similar game but with biology as the theme. Sacrifices (commensal) are needed to get different life forms on the table and the goal is to defeat your enemy. I really would appreciate some feedback on the game.

**What I’m looking for:** whether it's addictive enough that people would keep playing it, whether you would want to grind for unlocks like new cards, and whether you would consider paying for it in general if there were a campaign and multiplayer. If not, I would love to know what needs to be improved to hit those metrics. It's still a ways away mechanistically from being complete, but I thought I would just take a shot and get feedback now so I can target what needs to be improved sooner rather than later! Thank you for checking it out.

\*\*Free to Play Status:\*\*

\* \[ X \] Free to play  
\* \[X\] Demo/Key available  
\* \[  \]Paid

No subscription, no ads.

**Involvement:** Solo dev.

comments.body: So this is AI made or a crosspost?

replies.author: MDInformatics
replies.body: Yes, I’ll send over when I get home tomorrow!

comments.author: pimplurb
comments.body: When you drop a card it should tween rotation, not snap

replies.author: MDInformatics
replies.body: Good idea. This is the feedback I need. Thank you! Am open to anything else you got :)

replies.author: pimplurb
replies.body:
The perspective on the table and card placement feels a little off because the play area is more narrow on the far side but the cards aren't being adjusted the same way. I have seen shaders used for the fake 3d effect on cards to make them not perfectly square to give a perspective effect, not sure if that would work here. Might ruin readability 

The lift on hover and tool tips seem nice, I'm struggling with having my description boxes on hover be available but not in the way, but yours looks smooth

Is there a delay after end turn was pressed? Is that intentional? I didnt play it so I'm not sure if I feels natural but it looks a little off in the video

replies.author: MDInformatics
replies.body:
Got it. I’ll have to sit back and see how to mess with the actual card sizing with respect to the perspective. I’ll mess around with shading too and see what happens. Thank you for that. 

The delay isn’t intentional, but I do think there needs to be some spacing between end turn. I’m thinking about an effective transition but haven’t figured it out in a way that comes across as natural.

replies.author: pimplurb
replies.body:
By "shader" I mean the coding technique of applying a block of code to every pixel in an object 

https://godotshaders.com/shader/regionable-pseudo-3d/

This shader gives a 2d rectangle a 3d perspective feel. The example in the gif is a little extreme, you would only need a few degrees of tilt to make the cards look like they're flat on the table

replies.author: MDInformatics
replies.body: Ahh. Thank you! That makes plenty sense

comments.author: IamDroBro
comments.body:
heads up, the playable link in the post 404s, looks like the closing parenthesis got glued onto the url by reddit formatting. found the working one in the comments but a lot of people will bounce before doing that, worth editing the post if you can.

couldnt put real time in because of that, but on your pricing question: campaign plus multiplayer at like 5 bucks is an easy yes for an inscryption-shaped game, just keep some free version alive because free in the browser is why people click at all.

also since you asked about paying in general, im building a marketplace for browser games (posted about it here a couple days ago) and free-with-a-paid-upgrade card games are exactly the sweet spot. browser is an asset, not a compromise. art style is doing a lot of work btw, in a good way

replies.author: MDInformatics
replies.body:
Fixed the link. Thank you for the heads up!

I was thinking of pricing it around $8-10 assuming I expand it out. 

Whim looks cool, I think when I refine the demo I just might post it there. 

Also, I appreciate your kind words!
